chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya and Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: Do not pray the Maghrib prayer until you arrive at Jam', so pray Maghrib and the last Isha prayer there with one Adhan and two Iqamas. Descend into the valley floor on the right side of the road, near the Mash'ar. It is recommended for the first-timer to stand at the Sacred Mash'ar, tread upon it with his foot, and not pass the basins on the night of Muzdalifa.

And he should say: 'O Allah, this is Jam'. O Allah, I ask You to gather for me therein all encompassing goodness. O Allah, do not make me despair of the goodness which I ask You to gather for me in my heart. And I seek from You to make known to me what You made known to Your Guardians in this my station, and to protect me from all encompassing evil.'

And if you can stay awake during that night, then do so, for it has reached us that the doors of the sky are not closed that night for the voices of the believers, who have a humming sound like the humming of bees.
Allah, Exalted is His Praise, says: 'I am your Lord, and you are My servants. You have fulfilled My Right, and it is a Right upon Me to answer you.'
Thus, Allah removes from whom He wills their sins that night, and forgives whom He wills.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءَكَ: Your Guardians, referring to the Imams or divine favorites.
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرُ الْحَرَامُ: The Sacred Mash'ar (Monument), a key site for standing during Hajj.
key_terms.جَمْعٌ: Jam', a specific location in Muzdalifa where pilgrims combine prayers.
key_terms.جَوَامِعَ الْخَيْرِ: All-encompassing goodness, a concept in supplication asking for comprehensive divine blessings.
key_terms.دَوِيِّ النَّحْلِ: Humming of bees, a metaphor for the sound of believers' voices.
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْمُزْدَلِفَةِ: The night of Muzdalifa, the night spent between Mina and Muzdalifa.

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended prayers and supplications for the night of Muzdalifa in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the specific rites of Muzdalifa, emphasizing the consolidation of Maghrib and Isha prayers with a single Adhan and two Iqamas, a practice rooted in Shia jurisprudence. It prescribes descending to the valley near the Sacred Mash'ar for supplication, highlighting the night's unique spiritual atmosphere where the 'doors of heaven' remain open to the believers' voices, facilitating divine forgiveness and the accumulation of good deeds.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya and Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Do not Pray Al-Magrib until you come to Jam’a, so you should Pray at it Al-Magrib and Al-Isha the last, by one Azaan and two Iqamaas; and descend into the middle of the valley from the right of the road near to the monuments; and it is recommended for the first-timer that he pauses upon the Sacred Monuments, and he should set foot on it and should not exceed the basin on the night of Al-Muzdalifa.

And he should be saying, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! This is Jam’a. I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> that You<sup>azwj</sup> should Gather for me therein the entirety of the goodness. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Do not let me despair from the goodness which I ask you that You<sup>azwj</sup> Gather for me in my heart; and I seek to You<sup>azwj</sup> Introduce to me what You<sup>azwj</sup> Introduce Your<sup>azwj</sup> Guardians<sup>asws</sup> in this place of mine, and that You<sup>azwj</sup> Save me from the entirety of the evil’.

And if you are to stay awake during that night, then do so, for it has reached us<sup>asws</sup> that the Doors of the sky are not locked during the night for the voices of the Believers, humming like the humming of the bees.

Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Laudation is Saying: “I<sup>azwj</sup> am your Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and you all are My<sup>azwj</sup> servants. You have fulfilled My<sup>azwj</sup> Right, and it is a Right upon Me<sup>azwj</sup> that I<sup>azwj</sup> Answer you”.
Thus, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Degrades the sins from the ones whom He<sup>azwj</sup> Intends to Degrade from, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Forgives the ones whom He<sup>azwj</sup> Intends to Forgive for’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah and Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: (NOTE: Fatwa best explains the beginning of this Hadith.)“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

you must not perform al-Maghrib Salat (prayer) until you arrive at al-Jam‘ so that you can perform both al-Maghrib and al-‘Isha’ al-’Akhirah with one Adhan and two ’Iqamah. You must disembark in valley on the right side of the road near al-Mash‘ar. One who performs al-Hajj for the first time should stay in al-Mash‘ar al-Haram, walk on foot but must not pass Hiyaz in the night of al-Muzdalifah, and should say,

‘O Allah, this is an assembly. O Allah, I appeal before You to accumulate for me all goodness. O Allah, do not deprive me of the goodness for which I have appealed before You, and accumulate all of it in my heart. I appeal before You to make me learn what You have made Your friends to learn at this place, and keep me safe from all wickedness and evil.’

You should remain, if you can, that night awake. It has come to us that the doors of the heaven remain open that night for the voices of the believing people, who express a humming voice like honey bees.
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, says, ‘I am Your Lord and you are My servants. You have yielded to My rights and it is necessary for Me to answer your prayers.’
During that night Allah deletes the sins of whomever He wants and forgives whomever He decides to forgive.’”
